title: AI Agents Don't Read Your Policy Docs. They Hit Your APIs — Gravitee
talk_summary: A Gravitee CTO demos two live agents — one governed only by prompt/policy docs, one governed by a gateway with scoped identity and runtime policies — showing the prompt-only agent deletes bookings and leaks PII while the gateway blocks the same calls with 403s. He then shows gateway-level rate limiting, semantic caching, prompt-size/content blocking, and model routing as cost and safety controls.

takeaways.technique: Enforce permissions at the gateway, not in prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent identity is tightly scoped and tokens/JWT claims are only valid at runtime for the specific user task; unauthorized tool calls get 403 at the gateway before reaching the backend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the permissions would not were blocked at the gateway with a 403 kind of forbidden kind of code

takeaways.what_they_do: A buggy agent sending the same request 8 times gets the first 3 answered and the rest blocked at the gateway (3/minute), not after tokens are spent downstream.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can only do three every minute. So any more than three is blocked. They're not blocked at the LLM.
takeaways.numbers: 8 repeated requests, ~1000 tokens (~1 cent) ungoverned; 3/min cap governed

takeaways.technique: Semantic response cache at the gateway
takeaways.what_they_do: Similar prompts are served from a Redis-backed semantic cache with a tunable 0–1 similarity threshold, avoiding downstream LLM calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you get similar sounding prompts, you can serve it from a a built-in Reddis kind of store
takeaways.numbers: 5 identical prompts: ~1000 tokens uncached vs ~200 tokens cached

takeaways.what_they_do: Gateway rejects prompts over a token budget or irrelevant to the use case before any downstream LLM call, telling the caller to split into smaller steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Basically said this is too big blocked at the gateway level with a built-in policy that says think about cutting this up.
takeaways.numbers: 2000 input tokens / 312 output for a simple booking task

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of exposing a full MCP server (64 tools) to the model every call, they curate a fine-grained subset to cut context cost and blast radius.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our CRM we use exposes 64 tools for that MCP server. Dropping that into the model would expose huge context every time

takeaways.technique: Gateway model routing with spec translation
takeaways.what_they_do: Route to any downstream model by latency/cost/complexity and let the gateway translate between provider API specs, decoupling from a single hyperscaler.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can route to any downstream model depending on like um latency or cost or uh complexity
